title: Modular Shadow / p-adic Semilinearity Barrier
novelty_claim: Treat the problem as an obstruction theorem for exact value recurrences inside `floor(n r)`, using cross-modulus selector shadows instead of another Sturmian or bounded-partial-quotient classification. The claim is that any infinite homogeneous constant-coefficient recurrence subsequence should force eventually semilinear shadows modulo many primes, which generic irrational Beatty sequences do not support.
closest_prior_art: Skolem-Mahler-Lech style rigidity for linear recurrence sequences; classical Beatty and mechanical-word literature; Schaeffer-Shallit-Zorcic (2024) on quadratic-irrational Beatty decidability.
differentiation: This avoids the quadratic-only and symbolic-dynamics traps flagged by the falsifier. It targets exact arithmetic recurrences of subsequence values, requires predeclared selector classes, and uses multi-modulus consistency to kill prefix-fitting and post-selection artifacts before any structural theorem is attempted.
easiest_falsifier: Lock the definitions first, freeze selector families and recurrence order, then exhibit a non-rational irrational slope with an exact infinite recurrence subsequence whose selector has no stable cross-modulus semilinear shadow, or show that many generic irrationals survive the same modular screen.
evidence_plan: Lock the meanings of `r`, `subsequence`, and `homogeneous linear recurrence` before any theorem claim.
Run one pre-registered discriminator panel across rational, quadratic irrational, higher-degree Pisot, Salem, and transcendental slopes.
For fixed selector families and fixed recurrence orders, test whether exact candidates yield consistent eventual periodic or semilinear shadows modulo several primes and one prime-square follow-up.
Escalate only the irrational survivors to a structural explanation route; do not widen the search if the modular screen already fails.

title: Pisot Self-Matching Beyond Quadratic Units
novelty_claim: Promote higher-degree Pisot slopes as the first concrete irrational positive family, seeking exact homogeneous recurrences along companion-matrix or residue-class index sequences rather than rephrasing the standard Sturmian story.
closest_prior_art: Masakova-Pelantova on self-matching properties of Beatty sequences for quadratic units, plus substitution and cut-and-project work on linearly repetitive sets.
differentiation: This is a narrow exceptional-family claim, not a derivative `quadratic irrationals are special` thesis. It gives the cleanest positive mechanism if the champion screen leaves a small algebraic survivor class.
easiest_falsifier: Predeclare low-degree Pisot test cases and fixed companion-matrix style index constructions; if even the cubic Pisot base cases fail to produce exact eventual recurrences, demote the direction immediately.
evidence_plan: Start with named cubic Pisot slopes and one residue-class or companion-matrix index rule per slope.
Check exact identities of the form `floor(U_k r) = V_k + c` or exact recurrence closure of a fixed subsequence; reject near-misses from convergents.
Run the same fixed constructions on non-Pisot algebraic controls and Salem controls.
Promote only if the Pisot versus non-Pisot split is sharp and reproducible.

budget_envelope.research: 1 focused exceptional-family run; no untargeted selector mining

title: Generalized-Polynomial / LRS Intersection Rigidity
novelty_claim: Reframe the classification problem as an exact intersection question between Beatty generalized-polynomial sets and integer linear recurrence value sets, aiming to explain any irrational survivors through a shared arithmetic model rather than through word complexity.
closest_prior_art: Generalized-polynomial and bracket-word work such as Adamczewski-Konieczny, together with classical Beatty-sequence theory and standard linear recurrence sequence structure theory.
differentiation: This is the broadest unifying frame from the scouts, but it stays in reserve because the current novelty screen is too weak to support it as the first active claim. It is best used after the champion screen isolates genuine irrational survivors.
easiest_falsifier: Find a robust irrational positive example outside the expected algebraic or Pisot-type generalized-polynomial mechanisms, or show that the ordered subsequence problem cannot be reduced cleanly to Beatty-set membership under the locked definitions.
evidence_plan: Use the modular-screen champion to isolate real irrational survivors first.
For each survivor, test whether the selector and value sequence admit a common generalized-polynomial description.
Check explicitly whether the ordered-sequence formulation adds constraints beyond Beatty-set membership.
Attempt a classification statement only after the prior-art gap file has real differentiation evidence.
